notes:
Account overview: Arkstone designs routing and capacity optimization for last-mile logistics. Moving from small self-hosted infra to enterprise dedicated inference to meet SLAs for customer-facing chat and fast reranking pipelines. Key ask: guaranteed throughput and predictable tail latency under bursty load.

Recent interactions / timeline:
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (Ethan) — Arkstone product lead outlined need for sub-200ms 95th pct latency for short-chat queries; currently 95th ~420ms on general-purpose hosts.
- 2026-01-28: Security questionnaire submitted; SOC2 + KMS required. (drive link above).
- 2026-02-05: Demo of Redwood Dedicated; showed warm-pool behavior and graceful degradation on fallback models. SE attended: Priya.
- 2026-02-18: Technical deep-dive with infra (network/VPC) — Arkstone requires private peering and strict egress filtering; asked about private control plane option.
- 2026-02-25: Preliminary sizing workshop: Arkstone workloads — mix of chat (50% short) + reranking (30% heavy token-throughput) + embeddings for nightly reindexing. Baseline QPS estimate: 300 concurrent short-chat users with 200 token avg, and reranking bursts up to 1k requests/minute. Suggested starting reserved pool: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs with 2x warm-pool replicas.
- 2026-03-03: Price vs SLA negotiation (commercial) — Arkstone requests 99.9% availability SLA and 95th pct latency SLOs; requesting service credits for missed SLOs and a fast-response escalation path.
- 2026-03-09: Request for 2-hour stress test with warm-pool pre-warmed to validate scale-up time and queue behavior.

Technical notes from SE call (Priya):
- Autoscaling model preference: proactive scale-up based on queue length + predictive traffic model derived from historical telemetry; scale-down with aggressive cooldown for cost control but not below min warm pool size.
- Warm pools: Arkstone wants a guaranteed pre-warmed slot count (min 2 GPUs) to achieve cold-start <50ms for KV cache warmups. They are sensitive to per-warm-instance billing and want clear metering.
- Queueing behavior: prefer bounded request queue with priority lanes (high-priority chat vs low-priority batch embeddings). Need config for per-route max queue depth and backpressure signals to caller.
- Latency SLOs: target 95th <= 180ms for chat, P99 <= 400ms for reranking under baseline load; need documented degradation plan (fallback to cheaper model) when latencies breach.
- Throughput guarantees: require token/sec baseline for reranking flows; discussed reserved GPU planning to ensure steady throughput during spikes and scheduled nightly embeddings jobs.

Commercial / negotiation points:
- SLA credits frequency and calculation: Arkstone requests explicit credit formula tied to 95th/99th latency bands and per-window availability.
- Warm-pool costs: want option to convert warm pool hours to burst credits.
- Commitment term: exploring 12-24 month reservation with quarterly review and ability to adjust GPU mix after 6 months.

POC plan (agreed):
- 2026-03-15: Execute 2-hr dedicated capacity stress test (SE + Arkstone infra) with warm-pool prewarm, two traffic patterns (steady + burst). Objectives: observe scale-up latency, queue growth, tail latency percentiles, and KV cache warm-up timings.
- Deliverables: stress-test report, suggested reserved GPU count, recommended scale policies (scale-up thresholds, cooldowns), and SLA draft.

Sales notes / shorthand:
- Champion: Lina Morales, VP Product (likes deterministic SLAs).
- Economic sens: medium-high; willing to commit if unit economics saved vs self-host.
- Quote: initial ARR ask ~ $400k/yr but flexible depending on warm-pool billing model.

Open questions for Redwood team:
- Metering detail for warm-pool vs active usage (per-GPU-minute?).
- Can fallback models be automatically routed without significant config overhead? Need example routing policy.
- Support SLA for private control plane (is SLA identical to hosted?).

Next immediate actions: schedule the stress test (Ethan to confirm tooling), SE to provision test config and share runbook, commercial to prepare SLA draft + term options.
